data: Israeli Air Force / Israel Aerospace Industries (Shavit)
Israel's launch site: Shavit rockets put Ofeq satellites in retrograde orbit since 1988

Israeli Air Force base on the Mediterranean coast south of Tel Aviv, used jointly by the IAF and the Israel Space Agency as Israel's spaceport. Ofeq-1 on a Shavit rocket, launched on 19 September 1988, made Israel the eighth country with its own orbital launch capability. Facts from Wikipedia (Palmachim Airbase, Shavit, Ofeq) and GlobalSecurity; coordinates are Wikipedia's airbase point, not the launch pad itself.

Palmachim Airbase stands on the Mediterranean coast west of Yavne, about 12 km south of the Tel Aviv area. The Israeli Air Force and the Israel Space Agency operate it jointly as Israel's spaceport. Israel Aerospace Industries' three-stage solid-fuel Shavit rocket first flew from here on 19 September 1988, carrying Ofeq-1 into orbit and making Israel the eighth country able to launch its own satellite. Launching east would send stages over neighbouring states, so Shavit flies west over the sea into retrograde orbits, with Ofeq at 143 degrees inclination. At this latitude the Earth's rotation works against the rocket by about 1,420 km/h, which cuts payload. The Shavit is widely reported to be derived from the Jericho II missile. The base also hosts helicopter and drone squadrons and an Arrow missile battery.
